newsitem.title: BRAZIL: TENNIS-BRAZIL FIGHT BACK TO REDUCE DEFICIT AGAINST U.S..
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BRAZIL FIGHT BACK TO REDUCE DEFICIT AGAINST U.S..

text.p: Brazil fought their way back into their Davis Cup tie against the United States when they won the doubles on Saturday to reduce the North Americans' lead to 2-1.
Jaime Oncins and Gustavo Kuerten outplayed a nerve-racked Alex O'Brien and Richey Reneberg to win 6-2 6-4 7-5.

Reneberg, in particular, appeared intimidated by the 5,000-strong crowd who greeted the United States' pair with a chorus of whistling and played their usual samba drums and blew horns between points.

He had a nightmare match, losing his first four service games and making two unforced errors on successive points in the 11th game of the third set, allowing Brazil to break his serve again before the hosts wrapped up the rubber in the next game.
